overview: The file consists of a single “List of Papers” sheet rather than substantive correspondence. It cross-references telegram no. 261 from Japan, attributed to Ambassador Forbes and dated June 30, 1931, to decimal-file location 894.00 PR/43; an additional administrative notation ending in “20,000” is too corrupted by OCR to interpret reliably. Although the file title covers carrier pigeons, aerial navigation, government-controlled transportation, subsidies, and offenses aboard aircraft, none of those subjects is discussed on the surviving page.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Forbes telegram no. 261 from Japan
subfiles.about: The sheet directs readers to another decimal-file location for telegram no. 261 from Ambassador Forbes in Japan.
subfiles.summary: This administrative sheet records a reference to telegram no. 261 from Japan, attributed to Forbes and dated June 30, 1931. It directs the reader to file 894.00 PR/43 rather than reproducing or summarizing the telegram. A separate OCR-corrupted notation ends with the figure “20,000,” but its meaning cannot be established from the text.

interest: The sheet is useful chiefly as evidence of State Department filing practice and the dispersal of related material across the decimal file. It identifies a potentially relevant Forbes telegram that is absent from this bundle and supplies the file number needed to locate it. The gap between the broad subject heading and the minimal surviving contents may also help historians reconstruct missing, transferred, or cross-filed records.
